trigger: Real Environment C failure: the operator installed the Phase 3.8.6 whisper-enabled installer on a real Windows machine and launched it. Windows reported: "cip-desktop.exe - System Error: The code execution cannot proceed because libstdc++-6.dll was not found. Reinstalling the program may fix this problem." (screenshot evidence). This is a definitive, real installer-packaging defect, not speculation.

classification.windowsSystemDllsNote: Present on every stock Windows 10/11 x64 installation - never bundled
classification.nonSystemRuntimeDllsNote: The one real gap - whisper.cpp's C++ code is dynamically linked against it (confirmed via the actual linker invocation captured during Phase 3.8.6, which used -Wl,-Bdynamic ... -lstdc++)
classification.alreadyHandledByTauriNote: Tauri's own NSIS generation already copies this automatically (confirmed present in installer.nsi's main install section before this phase's changes) - untouched by this phase

transitiveDependencyInspection.method: x86_64-w64-mingw32-objdump -p run against each candidate DLL in turn, not assumed
transitiveDependencyInspection.conclusion: The full, closed transitive set of non-system runtime DLLs required is exactly three: libstdc++-6.dll, libgcc_s_seh-1.dll, libwinpthread-1.dll. No fourth DLL is needed (libwinpthread-1.dll has no further non-system dependencies).

dllSourceAndVerification.toolchainVariant: posix-threads - matches the toolchain variant actually used to build cip-desktop.exe this phase (see docs/phase-3-8-6-windows-whisper-build.md's mingw threading-model fix); using the win32-threads variant's copy instead would risk an ABI mismatch
dllSourceAndVerification.architectureBeforeStrip: PE32+ executable (DLL) (console) x86-64, for MS Windows, 20 sections

dllSourceAndVerification.toolchainVariant: shared between posix/win32 variants (winpthreads itself has no thread-model split)

architectureVerification: All three staged DLLs and cip-desktop.exe itself confirmed PE32+ x86-64 via file(1) before packaging - the build script (scripts/build-windows-whisper.sh) refuses to proceed if any staged DLL is not x86-64.

debugSymbolStripping.reasoning: The stock Ubuntu-packaged libstdc++-6.dll ships with full debug info (26MB) - stripping only removes debug sections, never code or the export table (verified: the import table of the stripped libstdc++-6.dll is byte-identical in content to the unstripped original, confirmed via objdump -p before/after)
